lines.para: Salazar’s Portugal stays neutral. Lisbon becomes the last way out of Europe at war: tens of thousands of refugees wait there for a visa, a ship, a seat on the Pan Am seaplane to New York.

In Estoril, the two sides share the grand hotels: the British at the Palácio, the Germans at the Atlântico. In the evening, everyone meets at the casino. They gamble, they drink, and above all, they listen.
